## Company Overview

Quilliam AI is the trading name of Quilliam AI Ltd, a UK private limited company registered in England and Wales (Companies House number 17151006), incorporated on 2026-04-11. Registered office: 25 Red Cove Close, St. Eval, Wadebridge, PL27 7GB. Sole director and shareholder: Levi Lachlan Quilliam.

Quilliam AI is based in Cornwall and works with UK businesses that want to move from scattered AI interest to working AI systems. The core positioning is simple: make AI clear, build the useful workflow, and train the team so the business owns the result.

Quilliam AI is not a strategy consultancy selling decks, and it is not a software team building impressive demos that nobody uses. The practical work is: understand the business, identify where AI has a business case, design the workflow, build the system, add controls, train the team, document the runbook, and leave the client with ownership.

## Positioning

Most businesses do not need more AI noise. They need one real workflow improved: lead follow-up, admin, support triage, reporting, document handling, internal knowledge, or customer communication. The commercial opportunity is not to buy every new AI tool. The opportunity is to decide where AI can safely help with work the business already does.

Quilliam AI turns AI into scoped, controlled business systems. That means choosing a workflow with a real owner, defining the trigger and context, connecting the right tools and data, building the automation or agent where useful, adding approval gates and logs, then training the team until the workflow becomes normal.

---

## Services

### AI Opportunity Analysis
AI Opportunity Analysis is for business owners who know AI should matter but do not know where to start. Quilliam AI reviews repeated work, current tools, team readiness, risks, and likely value. The output is a plain-English recommendation on what to do first, what needs preparation, and what should be ignored for now.

### Team Training
Team Training is for staff who need practical confidence using AI in real work. Quilliam AI trains people on role-specific examples, useful prompts, checking output, privacy boundaries, internal rules, and when to keep a human in control. The aim is not generic prompt tips. The aim is that staff know how to use AI safely and effectively in the work they already do.

### Supervised AI Agents and Automations
Supervised AI Agents are agents with jobs, boundaries, and controls. They can read from the right sources, prepare the next action, and escalate when confidence or risk demands it. Typical agents include lead qualification agents, support triage agents, research agents, internal knowledge agents, CRM hygiene agents, and operations reporting agents.

Quilliam AI does not treat autonomy as the starting point. Agents should earn trust before they earn autonomy. Controls can include limited permissions, scoped tool access, human approval for risky actions, test examples, logs, fallback paths, and named owners.

### AI Implementation
AI Implementation is for turning the best opportunities into working business systems. Quilliam AI redesigns repeated processes so AI can handle judgement-light work and humans keep important decisions. Typical workflows include lead intake, sales follow-up, customer support triage, weekly reporting, research packs, internal briefing, document intake, and admin handoffs across email, docs, CRM, and spreadsheets.

The workflow anatomy is: trigger, context, action, control. A trigger starts the process. Context pulls the right customer history, policy, examples, or documents. The action drafts, routes, classifies, updates, researches, or summarises. Control adds human approval, logging, and fallback paths.

---

## Case Study - VetVision AI

VetVision AI is a University of Nottingham spin-out using camera systems to monitor animal welfare across equine and dairy environments. Quilliam AI helped make the AI product easier to sell, onboard, operate, and improve through clearer positioning, website redesign, branded onboarding portals, farm and camera operations workflows, and internal AI implementation support.

The project brought two brands together under the VetVision AI name and rebuilt the website so the product quality was reflected in the public presence. Quilliam AI also created a branded onboarding portal to give end users a clearer start-to-finish experience, plus an operations workflow to help map farms and plan camera placement or replacement more clearly.

Reported outcomes include a site SEO score moving from roughly 40 to 95, stronger visibility across Google and AI search, increased visitor numbers, and increased lead flow.

---

## How It Works

### 1. Find the work worth fixing
Quilliam AI inspects repeated admin, slow handoffs, customer friction, reporting loops, and knowledge gaps that actually cost time or money. The output is a plain-English AI map: what to build now, what needs preparation, and what should be left alone.

### 2. Choose the first useful build
The best opportunity becomes a scoped build plan. This defines trigger, context, decision, action, approval, logging, fallback, owner, risk, and success measure. This prevents generic AI tool shopping and keeps the project tied to business value.

### 3. Build it around existing tools
Quilliam AI connects AI models to tools and data with supervision, permissions, tests, logs, and human approval where needed. The first version is intentionally focused, then hardened once it has been tested against real work.

### 4. Hand it to the team
The project is not finished when the demo works. Quilliam AI trains users, documents the workflow, names the owner, and reviews whether the system is being used. Success means the workflow becomes part of normal work.

---

## Ideal Client Profile

Strong fits include:
- Small and growing businesses with repeated admin, follow-up, reporting, or customer-support work
- Agencies and consultancies trying to improve delivery operations
- Startups and scale-ups building AI-native operating habits
- Teams inside larger organisations piloting AI adoption
- Founder-led businesses that want a senior person close to the work

The through-line is not industry or size. It is readiness to move from AI experiments to working systems.

Good project signals:
- The same kind of task happens every week
- The work has examples, rules, policies, or repeated patterns
- A real person owns the outcome
- The cost of delay or manual effort is already visible

## Founder - Levi Quilliam

Levi Quilliam is the founder and sole director of Quilliam AI Ltd. He holds a Bachelor's degree in Economics and a Graduate Certificate in Computer Science. He began his career at Deloitte in turnaround and restructuring, where he developed a practical understanding of how businesses operate and where inefficiencies hide. He then moved into technology, including work at Halter and XGX.AI.

Levi founded Quilliam AI because many businesses were buying AI tools, reading case studies, and watching webinars without turning that interest into usable systems. Quilliam AI closes that gap by identifying what matters, building it, and helping teams adopt it.

---

## Budget Guidance

Quilliam AI quotes by scope because useful AI work depends on the workflow, data, systems, risk, and handoff needs. Training usually starts from £500. Small implementation projects can sit around £2,000-£3,000, medium projects can range from £5,000-£50,000, and larger programmes are usually £50,000+. Ongoing support is available where a system needs monitoring, iteration, or managed improvement. Every paid engagement is scoped clearly before work starts.

---

## FAQs

### What does Quilliam AI do?
Quilliam AI helps UK businesses make sense of AI, build useful AI workflows, and train their teams to use them properly.

### What is an AI opportunity session?
An AI opportunity session is a focused first conversation where Quilliam AI looks at how a business works, where AI could remove drag, and which workflow is worth building first. The output is a practical recommendation, not a generic strategy deck.

### Do you train teams?
Yes. Training is tied to the workflows and agents being shipped. The aim is not generic AI literacy. The aim is that the team understands how to use, trust, and improve the system.

### Do you build automations?
Yes. Quilliam AI builds AI workflows, n8n automations, custom tools, API integrations, knowledge systems, and supervised agents where there is a real business case.

### How do you stop agents going wrong?
By designing for supervision: limited permissions, scoped tool access, human approval for risky actions, test examples, logs, fallback paths, and named owners.
